title: FP8 compute flag crashes on Apple Silicon MPS (--supports-fp8-compute)
detail:
> [!warning] Never pass --supports-fp8-compute on Apple Silicon — it crashes with ValueError.
The flag tells the runtime to use FP8 quantized matmul via torch._scaled_mm_v2. On MPS this operator is unsupported and falls back to CPU, where it crashes with `ValueError: Invalid scaling configuration` (mat_a is Byte, mat_b is Float8_e4m3fn). All models on this stack run bf16/fp16 natively — the flag is never needed. Remove it from any run.sh / launch script on MPS.

title: SeedVR2 offload_device must be 'none' (not 'cpu') on MPS
detail:
> [!warning] SeedVR2 offload_device='cpu' is rejected on MPS — must be 'none'.
SeedVR2's get_device_list() explicitly excludes 'cpu' on MPS-only systems because unified memory makes CPU offloading meaningless. Correct config: device=mps, offload_device=none, cache_model=False, blocks_to_swap=0, attention_mode=sdpa. Passing offload_device='cpu' fails device validation before generation starts.

title: No CUDA attention backends on Apple Silicon — SDPA only
detail:
> [!caution] SageAttention, Flash Attention, and xformers all require CUDA and will not work on MPS.
Use SDPA (scaled_dot_product_attention) only. Attempting to enable CUDA-only attention backends fails silently or crashes at the first attention op. This is a platform constraint of the whole MLX/MPS stack, not a per-model setting.

title: image purify (SeedVR2) is source-dependent — degrades already-sharp images
detail:
> [!warning] Run 'image purify' on soft/under-detailed images only — it degrades already-sharp ones.
实测: rescues soft images (overall 6→8 via detail+sharpness) but DEGRADES already-sharp ones (9→7). The skin-plastic artifact is unfixable by purify or restore (platform-level). Also: the VLM (Gemma) over-praises purify output — always visually verify the skin dimension rather than trusting the caption.

title: VAE decoder outputs [-1,1] — must *0.5+0.5 before clamp or image is crushed dark
detail:
> [!warning] Diffusers AutoencoderKL VAE decoders output pixels in [-1,1]; convert *0.5+0.5 BEFORE clamping to [0,1].
Otherwise the entire dark half of the image is crushed to 0 (~64% dark pixels vs ~20% expected, output looks extremely dark). Verified on the Flux2 Klein VAE port — SSIM jumped to 0.9999994 after the fix. METHOD LESSON: verify-e2e must decode to FINAL PIXELS and compare, not stop at the final latent (latent cos=0.988 passed but the range bug was invisible until pixels were compared). ZImage VAE decoder already does the +0.5 — check before reusing the pattern.

title: Manual argv-parse loop must advance index on EVERY branch or it hangs silently
detail:
> [!warning] A missed i++ in a manual argv loop = silent infinite hang, not a crash — looks like a slow model.
The -V vs -VV branch (`a.length > 1`) matched bare -V AND -VV and incremented i in NEITHER → every -V spun forever (even bun test hung). FIX: (1) gate the multi-char branch with a stricter length so bare flags fall through to an arm with i++; (2) counted/stacked flags: count = length-1. LESSON: in any argv-parse loop with `continue`, EVERY branch must advance the cursor exactly once. VERIFY with a zero-side-effect parser smoke (parsePiArgs([...]) in /tmp/*.mjs that prints DONE+exits) — if it doesn't terminate <1s, you have THIS bug.

title: Edit tool multi-edit is all-or-nothing — a single bad oldText drops ALL edits silently
detail:
> [!caution] The edit tool applies ALL edits[] or NONE — verify the result count after every multi-edit call.
If ANY edits[].oldText fails to match (even one), ALL edits are silently dropped — no partial apply, no per-edit error. Only detectable by verifying the total count after the call (e.g. 'grep name: | wc -l' showed 7 instead of 9). Mitigation: always verify multi-edit results with a grep/count, especially when changing tool registrations or imports.

title: Never top-level cd into python/ or bun/ subdirs — cwd persists and breaks paths
detail:
> [!warning] A top-level `cd <dir> && ...` is blocked by a PreToolUse hook for a reason — the Bash tool's cwd persists across calls.
Drifting out of the repo root breaks repo-root-relative paths (python/venv, run.py, dist/...). Always do ONE of: (1) wrap in a subshell `( cd ... && ... )` so cwd resets; (2) use tool-native --cwd/-C flags (`bun run --cwd <pkg>`, `git -C <dir>`); (3) use absolute paths from repo root. The python/venv is at repo-root `python/venv/` — running `cd python/mlx-movie-director && ../../python/venv/bin/python run.py` fails because the relative path breaks after cd.

title: Vendor submodules (mflux/ltx-2-mlx) cleared after branch/worktree switch → ModuleNotFoundError
detail:
> [!warning] After a branch or worktree switch, vendor submodules (mflux/ltx-2-mlx/ComfyUI) can be cleared → 'No module named mflux' Phase-4 VAE crash.
Fix = git submodule update --init --recursive. This is the single most common reason run.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError on the image/video path after a checkout/worktree switch. The sibling forks (../mflux, ../ltx-2-mlx) are REQUIRED and their PyPI versions lack needed modules (mflux.models.z_image, ltx_core_mlx).

title: Stale __pycache__ bytecode causes phantom pytest failures — clear before trusting results
detail:
> [!caution] Stale __pycache__ bytecode can cause phantom pytest failures that disappear after clearing the cache.
Always clear __pycache__ (find . -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +) before trusting a failing suite result, especially after switching branches or editing source. A 'failing' test that passes after cache clear was never a real failure — it was stale bytecode shadowing the edited source.

title: Streaming subprocess.Popen with proc.wait() blocks forever if the child hangs
detail:
> [!warning] `for line in proc.stdout` + proc.wait() blocks forever if the child hangs — replace with a deadline + communicate().
A streaming subprocess that reads stdout line-by-line then calls proc.wait() has no timeout: if the child hangs without exiting, the parent blocks indefinitely (request-slot exhaustion). Replace with: capture via proc.communicate(timeout=N) with a deadline, or a select-based reader with a watchdog. This is the root cause of indefinite hangs in subprocess-orchestrated generation steps.

title: Filename tokens use %year%-%month%-%day%, NOT %date:...%
detail:
> [!tip] Use %year%-%month%-%day% for filename date tokens — the %date:...% form does not work.
The correct ComfyUI-style filename tokens for dates are the explicit %year%-%month%-%day% (or %hour%/%minute%). The %date:...% token format is not supported and silently produces wrong/empty filename segments.

title: resolveVault Tier-2 reads the Obsidian app open vault — can't fail deterministically in tests
detail:
> [!warning] pi-obsidian's resolveVault(cwd) has a Tier-2 fallback that resolves the REAL open Obsidian app vault.
Implication: you CANNOT make resolveVault fail by just clearing OB_VAULT_PATH on a dev machine with Obsidian installed — Tier-2 resolves the real open vault and the call succeeds with the WRONG vault. To test the vault-resolution-FAILURE path, inject a throwing resolver via a test seam (pi-knowledge-card exports __setVaultResolverForTest) rather than manipulating env vars. Also: resolveVault finds the run-dir config only when cwd is the REPO ROOT — tools must pass ctx.cwd, not process.cwd() of the package.

title: (cfg as any).x when AppConfig declares x? is a papered-over cast — drop it
detail:
> [!warning] `(cfg as any).x` when AppConfig already declares `x?` is a papered-over cast that hides the real optional typing.
Drop the cast and use the typed access (cfg.x) — the `as any` defeats the optional typing and masks cases where the field is genuinely undefined. This is a recurring smell in Swift/TS config plumbing where a lazy cast papers over a real optional-handling gap.

title: structured/*.jsonl KB was DESTRUCTIVELY overwritten each knowledge:learn run
detail:
> [!warning] The structured KB (avoid/lora-insights/params/strategies/examples) was DESTRUCTIVELY overwritten on every knowledge:learn run → the self-learning loop forgot everything.
Root cause: per-run write instead of merge. Fix = mergeByKey accumulation in knowledge-db.ts so each run ADDS to the existing KB rather than replacing it. Any 'the loop forgot what it learned' symptom in a knowledge-accumulation pipeline is this overwrite-vs-merge class of bug.

title: Never commit package-lock.json — bun.lock is canonical in this Bun workspace
detail:
> [!caution] This is a Bun workspace monorepo (isolated linker + globalStore via bunfig.toml); bun.lock is the canonical lockfile.
package-lock.json is gitignored. If one appears (e.g. an editor/tool regenerates it), DELETE it — do not adapt the code to it. Add deps with `bun add` (writes bun.lock), never `npm install` (writes package-lock.json). Committing package-lock.json creates a divergent lockfile that confuses CI/installs.

title: python/venv is NOT auto-created on fresh clone — run.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError: mlx
detail:
> [!warning] On a fresh clone (or after git clean) python/venv is ABSENT and run.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError: mlx.
The venv is gitignored and per-machine. Recreate on demand: `uv venv python/venv --python 3.12` then `uv pip install -r python/mlx-movie-director/requirements.txt --python python/venv/bin/python`, then `bash scripts/setup-repo-deps.sh` for the sibling-fork deps (mflux/ltx-2-mlx). The sibling venvs (whisper-venv, vision-venv) back ONLY the GUI Item-I adapters, NOT the full generation stack.

title: GUI dev port is per-worktree (not always 3099) — discover with bun run gui:port
detail:
> [!tip] The GUI dev server port is per-worktree — don't assume 3099.
The primary worktree (real .git) uses 3099; each linked worktree derives a stable port from its path (lib/worktree.ts). Run `bun run --cwd bun-apps/gui-movie-director gui:port` for yours; `--all` lists every server. Kill a stuck server by its discovered port (`lsof -ti :<port> | xargs kill -9`). Use `bun run dev` (hot reload), NOT `bun run start` (no file watching).

title: transformers must be <5 or mlx_lm AutoTokenizer.register breaks
detail:
> [!warning] requirements.txt pins transformers<5 because transformers 5.x breaks mlx_lm's AutoTokenizer.register.
Both sibling forks (mflux, ltx-2-mlx) leave transformers unpinned, so after installing them editable, scripts/setup-repo-deps.sh RE-ASSERTS transformers<5 at the end. If you see AutoTokenizer.register errors after a dep install, the pin got clobbered by a sibling fork's unpinned transformers.

title: Branches deleted at PR-merge time (SOP #320) — run stale-branches.sh after every merge
detail:
> [!tip] Branches are deleted at PR-merge time per SOP #320, not left to accumulate.
Enforcement is one command: run `./scripts/stale-branches.sh` after every merge (and at cycle start) — it lists branches outside the keep-set (main / current / worktree-checked-out / open-PR), each annotated with PR state. `--prune` deletes them; expect 0 stale on a clean repo. Post squash-merge: detach HEAD before local delete (set 2026-07-06), to avoid the worktree-main conflict.
